title: Eliminate capacitor and access transistor: vertical 3D CCD charge-packet memory
idea: Eliminate both the per-bit capacitor and the per-bit access transistor: store bits as charge packets in the potential wells of a vertical oxide-semiconductor channel wrapped by 64-128 stacked gate tiers (3D-NAND-style), and clock them like a CCD to one sense node at the top of each string. A 4-phase clock at 2-4 GHz moves a packet one tier per phase, so a 64-tier string gives ~10-30 ns average access plus burst streaming.
why: Attacks fact 2 (no manufacturable 3D cell) and fact 4 by reusing the mature 3D-NAND channel-hole process with no capacitor and one transistor per string; potential 5-10x bits/mm2 at 64+ tiers; retention set by well dark current, refresh happens naturally as packets recirculate.

title: Eliminate static storage: recirculating magnon delay-line loops hold bits in flight
idea: Eliminate the stationary storage element: bits circulate as spin-wave packets (wavelength ~50-100 nm) in 100-um closed YIG or CoFeB waveguide rings, with one magnetoelectric transducer per ring that regenerates and taps the stream. A ring holds ~1-2 kbit with ~50 ns average latency; storage is travel time, not a held state.
why: Removes capacitor, retention and refresh (facts 1, 3) because regeneration is part of circulation; no per-bit lithographic cell, only a waveguide ring; density today ~10x below DRAM, so the target is streaming KV/activation buffers at aJ-per-bit hold energy.

title: Eliminate junction leakage: nano-electromechanical relay seals each storage node
idea: Eliminate the semiconductor access junction: each capacitor connects to the bitline through a 20-nm electrostatic nano-relay (vertical cantilever across a vacuum gap) that touches only during access; when open, the leakage path is a physical gap, so node leakage drops from ~13 fA to effectively zero. Relays switch in ~1-5 ns at this size, with Ru or carbon contacts for high cycle counts.
why: Kills fact 3 (refresh = 16-33% idle power, 10-20% bandwidth) and lets Cs shrink 3-5x because only sensing, not retention, sets Cs, cutting the AR-75 pillar (fact 1); contact endurance toward 1e15 cycles is the risk.

title: Eliminate dielectric thickness limits: solid-electrolyte double-layer nanocapacitor storage node
idea: Eliminate the conventional capacitor dielectric: the storage node is a nano-electrode against a thin solid ion conductor (protonic phosphosilicate or LiPON) with blocking electrodes, so the sub-nm Helmholtz double layer (~20-40 uF/cm2) supplies the capacitance without any faradaic reaction. That is 2-4x the capacitance per area of ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 at EOT 0.4 nm, so a 5 fF node needs AR ~20-30 instead of 75.
why: Attacks fact 1 (charge wall) and fact 4 (fewer and shallower HAR etches); risk is double-layer charging time (<10 ns needed at nm scale) and self-discharge.

title: Eliminate stored charge: bistable buckled nanobeam holds the bit mechanically
idea: Eliminate charge as the information carrier: each cell is a pre-compressed 10x60 nm SiC or SiN nanobeam that buckles up or down into two elastic energy minima; a wordline electrostatic pulse snaps it over in ~1 ns (GHz resonance) and capacitive sensing reads its position non-destructively. No leakage can erase a mechanical state, so the capacitor and refresh both vanish.
why: Removes facts 1, 3 and 8 (non-destructive read); nonvolatile at zero hold power; contact-free flexing can exceed 1e15 cycles; density ~6-8F2 per layer and stackable.

title: Eliminate static states: nanomechanical parametrons store bits as oscillation phase
idea: Eliminate the static bistable well: each cell is a high-Q nanomechanical or LC resonator pumped at 2f by a shared line, which forces it to oscillate at f in one of two phases (0 or pi), reviving Goto's 1950s parametron at GHz. A small injection seeds the phase on write, a mixer reads it, and the pump continuously restores amplitude so the bit cannot decay.
why: Replaces refresh (fact 3) and destructive read (fact 8) with continuous parametric regeneration; hold energy is the shared pump (~nW per kbit for high-Q resonators); risks are resonator density and pump crosstalk.

title: Eliminate net magnetization: antiferromagnetic Mn3Sn bits read by anomalous Hall
idea: Eliminate the ferromagnet, the fixed layer and the MgO tunnel barrier: store the bit in the octupole order of the noncollinear antiferromagnet Mn3Sn, switched by spin-orbit torque from a heavy-metal underlayer in ~100 ps, and read it from its large anomalous Hall voltage in a simple Hall cross. With no stray field, cells pack at ~10 nm pitch without coupling.
why: Nonvolatile and refresh-free (fact 3), immune to charge-coupling disturb (fact 9); the stack shrinks from ~15 sputtered layers to ~2, cutting tool time; risk is the uV-scale Hall signal needing local gain.

title: Eliminate the separate capacitor: ferroelectric-semiconductor channel stores the bit itself
idea: Eliminate both the capacitor and the gate stack: make the channel from a ~3-nm ferroelectric semiconductor (alpha-In2Se3) whose locked in-plane/out-of-plane polarization modulates its own conductance by 1e3-1e5, so one device is both storage and access, with a non-destructive read.
why: Collapses 1T1C into one ~4F2 device, removing the capacitor wall (fact 1) and refresh (fact 3); stackable in BEOL below 400 C; risk is retention and endurance beyond 1e12 cycles.

title: Eliminate thermal generation leakage: wide-bandgap SiC or GaN storage junctions
idea: Eliminate silicon's thermal generation current: build the storage node and access junction in 4H-SiC or GaN (3.3-3.4 eV), where intrinsic carrier density is ~1e-8 cm-3 vs ~1e10 in Si, so junction and GIDL leakage fall by many orders of magnitude; 1990s SiC DRAM test cells already held charge for hours or more at room temperature.
why: Stretches retention from 64 ms to hours (fact 3), letting Cs drop to ~1 fF and the pillar to AR ~15 (fact 1); leans on the U.S.-strong SiC power-device supply chain; risk is SiC lithographic scaling and defect density.

title: Eliminate analog sensing: Coulomb-blockade dots hold quantized electron counts
idea: Eliminate the continuous charge level: store 0, 1, 2 or 3 extra electrons on a ~2-nm silicon or metal nanodot whose charging energy (>150 meV, ~6 kT) quantizes the stored charge, so each cell holds 2 bits as discrete states read by an integrated single-electron-transistor electrometer.
why: 2 bits per tiny cell (fact 1, density) with attojoule writes (fact 10); thick barriers make it refresh-free; risk is room-temperature operation needing sub-2-nm uniformity and offset-charge noise.

title: Eliminate up-down polarization: polar-vortex chirality bits in oxide superlattices
idea: Eliminate the up/down polarization picture: in PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattices, polarization curls into vortices or polar skyrmions whose handedness is a topologically protected bit, written by a curl-shaped field from split electrodes and read through its chirality-dependent (gyrotropic) electrical response.
why: Topological protection gives nonvolatility with no net polarization reversal (low fatigue) and ~10-nm bits; attacks refresh (fact 3) and density; electrical chirality readout is unproven.

title: Eliminate stored electrons: nanosecond protonic channel bits in tungsten-free oxides
idea: Eliminate stored electrons: the bit is the proton content of a 10-nm oxide channel (WO3, or MoO3 to avoid tungsten), pumped in or out of a phosphosilicate-glass electrolyte by nanosecond pulses, as protonic programmable resistors have shown; the result is a nonvolatile conductance read with tiny current.
why: Nonvolatile and refresh-free (fact 3), BEOL compatible, writes under 2 V (fact 10); risks are endurance toward 1e15 and ionic drift.

title: Eliminate atomic motion: hidden charge-density-wave states as purely electronic bits
idea: Eliminate any motion of atoms or ions: a picosecond electrical pulse switches a nano-patch of 1T-TaS2 from its commensurate insulating state into a metastable 'hidden' metallic CDW domain state; the bit is an electronic ordering pattern with 1e2-1e3 resistance contrast, erased by a longer pulse.
why: ps writes at fJ energies (fact 10) and non-destructive read (fact 8); hidden states are stable only at low temperature today, so the bet is room-temperature stabilization by strain or doping.

title: Eliminate the 64-ms retention spec: ephemeral sub-femtofarad cells for transient tensors
idea: Eliminate the assumption that every bit must survive 64 ms: build a memory class whose storage node is a planar ~0.5 fF capacitor with no pillar and ~100 us retention, used only for AI activations, KV-cache spill and gradients that are overwritten within microseconds; the controller tags allocations by lifetime and never refreshes them.
why: Removes the AR 60-75 pillar (facts 1, 4) for a large share of AI traffic; ~2-3x cheaper per bit for the ephemeral tier with zero refresh energy (fact 3).

title: Eliminate the metal storage node: polyoxometalate clusters as multi-electron reservoirs
idea: Eliminate the electrode-plus-dielectric capacitor: graft one molybdenum- or vanadium-based polyoxometalate cluster per cell (no tungsten), which reversibly accepts 2-8 electrons at discrete, well-separated redox potentials, gated by an oxide-semiconductor access transistor; each redox state is one level, giving 2-3 bits per cell.
why: A 1-2 nm molecular storage node breaks the capacitor wall (fact 1) and multi-level raises density 2-3x; risks are redox kinetics under 10 ns and cycle endurance.

title: Eliminate charge storage: spin-crossover molecules hold bits in spin state
idea: Eliminate charge: a thin film of Fe(II)-triazole spin-crossover molecules switches between low-spin and high-spin states, with ~10% volume change and a large permittivity shift, inside a room-temperature hysteresis loop; a strain pulse from a piezoelectric gate flips it and capacitive sensing reads it.
why: Bistable at room temperature with no leakage-driven decay (fact 3) at molecular density; risks are electrical switching speed (ns shown only optically) and fatigue.

title: Eliminate the oxide capacitor: band-offset germanium quantum-well hole pocket
idea: Eliminate the external capacitor: grow a 5-nm SiGe or Ge quantum well beneath a vertical Si access channel so its ~300-500 meV valence-band offset traps holes as the stored bit, shifting the channel threshold; a heterobarrier rather than a junction sets retention, 10-100x longer than plain floating-body cells.
why: Capacitor-less ~4F2 cell with retention near the 64 ms spec (facts 1, 3), epitaxial with no HAR capacitor etch; risk is band-to-band generation in Ge.

title: Eliminate destructive read: erasable conductive ferroelectric domain walls as bits
idea: Eliminate charge-sharing readout: in single-crystal LiNbO3 thin-film nanocells, a field pulse writes or erases a charged, conducting domain wall bridging two side electrodes in ns; reading is a small current through the wall (on/off ~1e3) that leaves the polarization undisturbed.
why: Non-destructive read removes the 128x overfetch and restore cost (fact 8) and refresh (fact 3); risks are scaling below 20 nm and wall-pinning variation.

title: Eliminate the storage-node conductor: retention-designed charge traps in nanolaminate dielectrics
idea: Eliminate the conductive storage node and its capacitor: store charge in a band of engineered traps (e.g., Ti dopants in Al2O3 tuned to ~1.0 eV depth) behind a 1.5-nm direct-tunneling oxide, so writes take ~10 ns at under 2 V and thermal emission gives seconds-to-minutes retention, a deliberately leaky flash sized for DRAM duty.
why: Removes the pillar capacitor (fact 1) and cuts refresh 100-1000x (fact 3); direct tunneling avoids Fowler-Nordheim wear; risk is trap generation capping endurance below 1e12.

title: Eliminate the solid channel: vacuum field-emission access to storage nodes
idea: Eliminate solid-state leakage: connect each storage node through a sealed 10-nm vacuum nano-gap with a sharp field-emission tip; at hold bias the Fowler-Nordheim current is effectively zero because there is no semiconductor and no generation, while a few-volt access pulse across the gap conducts uA in picoseconds.
why: Retention limited only by dielectric leakage (hours), so refresh disappears (fact 3); radiation hard; risks are tip wear, work-function drift and 3-5 V access voltage (fact 10).

title: Eliminate the solid storage medium: electrowetting nanodroplet position bits
idea: Eliminate solid-state storage: each cell is a sealed 30-nm pore holding a liquid-metal or ionic-liquid nanoplug that electrowetting moves between its top and bottom halves; capillary pinning holds it without power, and the plug position changes the cell capacitance 5-10x for readout.
why: Nonvolatile and refresh-free with no crystal-lattice wear-out (fact 3); viscous motion over ~10 nm might take 10-100 ns, which is the speculative part.

title: Eliminate channel charge transport for writes: caged-ion fullerene dipole bits
idea: Eliminate pushing charge through a channel: use endohedral fullerenes (Li+@C60) whose caged ion sits off-center in one of two positions, forming a switchable molecular dipole; a crossbar field flips the ion inside its cage in ~ps, and an underlying 2D-channel transistor senses the dipole.
why: 1-nm nonvolatile bit with ps writes and no lattice fatigue (facts 1, 3, 10); risks are room-temperature stability of the off-center state and readout signal size.

title: Eliminate full magnetization reversal: single skyrmion presence-absence in nanodots
idea: Eliminate full magnetization reversal: in a 20-nm Co/Pt/Ir multilayer dot with strong DMI, the bit is the presence or absence of one skyrmion, nucleated or annihilated by a voltage-controlled-anisotropy pulse and read through noncollinear magnetoresistance in a vertical tunnel stack.
why: ~10x lower write current than STT-MRAM, nonvolatile (fact 3) and dense; risk is thermal stability of 20-nm skyrmions at room temperature.

title: Eliminate refresh with liquid-nitrogen cooling instead of helium cryogenics
idea: Eliminate refresh and the tall capacitor by running DRAM at 77 K, cooled with liquid nitrogen (an air-separation product, not helium): junction and GIDL leakage fall by >1e6, retention goes from 64 ms to hours, and Cs can drop from ~5 fF to ~1-2 fF, a planar or AR-15 capacitor. Rack-level LN2 immersion loops use no rare gas at any step.
why: Removes refresh power (16-33% of idle, fact 3), wire resistance falls ~5x (fact 5), and the smaller capacitor drops the AR-75 etch (fact 1); the helium ban pushes cooling to N2, the cheapest cryogen; cooling overhead is offset by lower power.

title: Eliminate stored charge: 77-K YBCO persistent-current loops as bits
idea: Eliminate charge storage: the bit is the direction of a persistent supercurrent in a ~100-nm YBCO nano-loop broken by a grain-boundary Josephson junction, written by a current pulse and read by an adjacent nano-SQUID. YBCO superconducts at 92 K, so LN2 rather than helium is enough, and it is grown by MOCVD in O2 with no argon sputtering.
why: Zero static dissipation and ps switching (facts 3, 10) with no leakage at all; the ban on liquid helium forces high-Tc materials; risks are junction reproducibility and loop inductance limiting density to ~0.1 um2 per bit.

title: Eliminate capacitor-hole etching: self-ordered anodic alumina pores become storage nodes
idea: Eliminate the HAR plasma etch, which needs helium backside cooling and argon-diluted plasmas: CVD aluminum from dimethylaluminum hydride (not argon sputtering), then anodize it in oxalic acid, guided by nanoimprinted dimples aligned to the transistor grid, to grow straight 20-30 nm pores at AR 100+. ALD with N2 purge and electroless Ru turn each pore into one capacitor.
why: Attacks fact 1 (AR 115 becomes cheap because pore depth is just anodizing time) and fact 4 (removes the costliest etch tool) using abundant materials; risk is pore registration to transistors at 30 nm pitch.

title: Eliminate dielectric deposition: anodically grow the capacitor dielectric from its electrode
idea: Eliminate the deposited dielectric: form a Nb or Ta bottom electrode by CVD or electroless plating, then anodize it so a dense Nb2O5 (k~40) or Ta2O5 (k~25) film grows inward at ~2 nm/V, perfectly conformal at any aspect ratio, with thickness set by voltage to ~0.1 nm. No plasma, no sputter targets and no rare-gas ALD purges are used.
why: Conformality at AR >100 is automatic (fact 1) and the dielectric tool is a wet cell (fact 4); anodic growth thickens fastest at weak spots, trimming the leakage tail (fact 3); risk is lower k than the best ZAZ stacks at equal leakage.

title: Eliminate plasma etch: metal-assisted chemical etching carves AR-150 capacitor holes
idea: Eliminate plasma etching: lay a perforated gold or silver catalyst mesh (nanoimprint lift-off or electroless plating) and immerse in HF/H2O2 at room temperature, so the catalyst sinks vertically and carves 25-nm holes in silicon at AR >150 with smooth walls in minutes; ALD liner and electrode turn the holes into capacitor shells.
why: Breaks the AR-75 ceiling (fact 1 asks for AR 115) without helium-cooled chucks or argon plasma, replacing a $10M+ etch tool with a wet bench (fact 4); risks are catalyst wandering and metal contamination.

title: Eliminate storage-node lithography: transistors electroplate their own capacitor towers
idea: Eliminate the storage-node mask and etch: after building the access transistors, immerse the wafer in a plating bath and turn on every wordline so each working transistor's drain contact sources current and plates its own Ni/Ru nanotower; then add ALD dielectric (N2 purge) and top plate. No argon-sputtered seed is needed because the drains are the seeds.
why: Self-aligned capacitor with no litho layer and no etch (fact 4); towers reach AR 100+ by plating time (fact 1); dead transistors grow no node, giving a built-in yield screen; risk is plating uniformity across billions of sites.

title: Eliminate excimer lithography: block-copolymer cylinders template every storage node
idea: Eliminate ArF and EUV exposure for the cell array, since excimer lasers need neon, argon and krypton and EUV drive lasers use helium: a high-chi block copolymer on a sparse UV-LED-exposed chemical guide self-assembles into a hexagonal 24-nm-pitch cylinder lattice. Sequential infiltration synthesis (TMA/H2O, N2 purge) turns the cylinders into AlOx hard masks for the storage nodes.
why: Removes 2-3 litho layers from the cell array (fact 4: 5-7 EUV layers today), and hexagonal packing fits ~15% more nodes per area; risk is reaching defect density under 1/cm2.

title: Eliminate tall pillars: Langmuir-Blodgett perovskite nanosheets give planar high-k capacitors
idea: Eliminate the 3D pillar: transfer 3-5 monolayers of exfoliated Ca2Nb3O10 or Sr2Nb3O10 perovskite nanosheets from a water trough by Langmuir-Blodgett onto storage electrodes, giving a 5-10 nm dielectric with k~150-200 that stays high when thin because there is no dead layer; a 5 fF cell then needs only a short cup.
why: Meets the fact-1 k~70 target with ~2-3x the capacitance per area of ZAZ, cutting AR to ~25 (fact 4); room-temperature water processing uses no vacuum gases; risks are leakage at sheet edges and conformality.

title: Eliminate refresh: bistable tunnel-diode pair holds each bit statically
idea: Eliminate refresh: put two Si/SiGe resonant interband tunnel diodes in series on each storage node, so their negative-differential-resistance curves cross at two stable node voltages (a Goto-pair latch) with ~pA standby current per cell, while one access transistor reads and writes as in DRAM. The diodes are grown by RPCVD in hydrogen carrier with in-situ B/P delta doping, so no rare gases are used.
why: A static cell with a 1T footprint plus a vertical diode stack drives refresh energy and bandwidth loss (fact 3) to zero and needs only a small capacitor (fact 1); risk is peak-to-valley ratio uniformity at nm scale.

title: Eliminate linear-only dielectrics: built-in-biased antiferroelectric zirconia storage capacitor
idea: Eliminate the assumption that the capacitor dielectric must be linear: use antiferroelectric ZrO2 between asymmetric ALD electrodes (TiN from TiCl4/NH3 vs RuO2, all with N2 purge, not argon) whose work-function difference biases the film onto the steep part of its double loop, so field-induced polarization adds 2-3x charge inside a 0-1 V window without full domain reversal.
why: Effective k~70-100 meets the fact-1 target without AR 115, using an ALD-only, rare-gas-free stack; risks are endurance of partial AFE switching (>1e15 needed) and temperature drift.

title: Eliminate the access transistor: ALD tunnel-diode crossbar storage capacitors
idea: Eliminate the transistor: put each storage capacitor at a crossbar intersection behind an asymmetric metal-insulator-metal tunnel diode (ALD Al2O3/Ta2O5/TiO2 nanolaminate with barrier heights tuned for a >1e8 current ratio between 1.5 V and 0.3 V), so half-selected cells see too little bias to leak; lines are ALD TiN plus electroplated Cu, with no argon sputtering, and the 4F2 cell stacks in 8+ BEOL layers.
why: A stacked 4F2 crossbar attacks density and capital (facts 2, 4) and removes the leaky transistor; risk is holding diode leakage near fA, or refresh returns at a slower rate.

title: Eliminate sputtered magnetic stacks: electroplated vertical racetracks in alumina pores
idea: Eliminate per-bit cells and argon-sputtered MTJ stacks: electroplate Co/Ni nanowires with composition modulated every 20 nm (built-in pinning notches) into 2-5 um anodic alumina pores, and shift magnetic domain walls past one read/write head at each pore base with current pulses; each pore holds ~100 bits.
why: 10-100x density per footprint without building tiers (fact 2), plating instead of PVD, refresh-free and nonvolatile; risks are domain-wall shift reliability and current density.

title: Eliminate current-driven writes: magnetoelectric bismuth ferrite flips electroplated nanomagnets
idea: Eliminate write current and the tunnel junction: a BiFeO3 layer grown from solution or by PLD in O2 switches its coupled ferroelectric and antiferromagnetic order at sub-volt bias and drags an exchange-coupled electroplated CoFe nanomagnet with it; the bit is read from the CoFe's anomalous Hall voltage, so no MgO barrier or fixed layer is sputtered with argon.
why: aJ-scale writes break the CV2 floor through low voltage (fact 10), nonvolatile (fact 3), rare-gas-free stack; risks are BFO switching endurance and ns speed at scale.

title: Eliminate holding energy: van der Waals stiction latches nanocantilever bits
idea: Eliminate any energy source for holding state: a 10-nm graphene or ALD-TiN cantilever is pulled electrostatically onto a pad where van der Waals adhesion keeps it stuck (bit 1) with zero power, and a second pull-off electrode peels it free (bit 0); contact resistance reads the state. The sacrificial ALD oxide is removed by vapor HF, so no rare gases are used.
why: Turns the classic MEMS failure, stiction, into the storage mechanism: nonvolatile, leak-free and refresh-free (fact 3); risks are adhesion variability and contact endurance.

title: Eliminate vacuum-deposited ferroelectrics: solution-grown croconic-acid proton-transfer bits
idea: Eliminate inorganic, vacuum-deposited ferroelectrics: grow the room-temperature organic ferroelectric croconic acid (Ps ~20 uC/cm2) from solution inside cell pores, where polarization reverses by collective proton transfer along hydrogen bonds, a light-particle switch that needs small fields and no oxygen-vacancy motion.
why: Nonvolatile storage at low coercive voltage (fact 10) made by solution casting with no process gases; proton transfer avoids the vacancy-driven fatigue of HZO; risks are thermal budget, thin-film quality and BEOL integration.

title: Eliminate deposited tunnel oxides: ligand shells set nanocrystal storage barriers
idea: Eliminate the deposited tunnel oxide: spin-cast monodisperse 4-nm Si or InP nanocrystals as storage nodes whose organic ligand shell (C8 vs C12 alkyl chains) is the tunnel barrier, so barrier width is fixed molecularly to ~0.1 nm and retention from ms to s is chosen by ligand length; writes tunnel in ns at ~1 V, with no vacuum tool or gas.
why: Removes ALD/PVD steps and the capacitor (fact 1), and molecularly uniform barriers collapse the retention tail (fact 3); risks are ligand degradation under repeated tunneling and film packing defects.

title: Eliminate plasma in 3D cells: vapor-HCl lateral etch carves horizontal capacitors
idea: Eliminate plasma steps in a 3D DRAM stack: grow 30-60 Si/SiGe bilayers by hydrogen-carrier CVD, cut slits, then use highly selective vapor HCl at 600-700 C to remove SiGe sideways and open the horizontal capacitor cavities and channel spaces in one gas-only, plasma-free step before ALD dielectric and electrode.
why: Attacks fact 2 (a manufacturable 3D cell needs 26+ tiers) by replacing many helium-cooled, argon-diluted HAR plasma etches with a thermal chemical etch; risks are selectivity across 60 tiers and strain-induced bowing.

title: Eliminate vacuum high-k deposition: hydrothermal conversion of titania shells to SrTiO3
idea: Eliminate ALD of exotic high-k: coat capacitor holes with a few nm of TiO2, then convert it in place in an aqueous Sr(OH)2/Ba(OH)2 bath at 150-200 C into crystalline SrTiO3 or (Ba,Sr)TiO3 (k~100-300), conformal because the ion exchange follows the TiO2 template.
why: k well above the fact-1 target of 70 lets AR fall to ~30-40; a water-based step with no plasma or rare gases cuts tool cost (fact 4); risks are leakage below 8 nm and crystallization defects.

title: Eliminate metal electrodes: degenerate epitaxial silicon plates replace TiN and tungsten
idea: Eliminate sputtered TiN and tungsten electrodes: form both capacitor plates and node contacts from in-situ phosphorus-doped (>1e21 cm-3) epitaxial Si or SiGe grown with hydrogen carrier, so there are no metal targets, no argon PVD and no tungsten; at that doping the depletion penalty is under ~5% of capacitance.
why: Removes a tungsten dependence (China ~80%) and argon PVD chambers (scarce-resource axis), and same-tool epitaxy cuts steps; risks are plate resistance slowing RC and depletion at high field.

title: Eliminate deep etching: self-rolling strained nanomembranes become swiss-roll capacitors
idea: Eliminate any deep etch: deposit a strained SiNx bilayer by SiH4/NH3/N2 PECVD (no helium or argon dilution) topped with electrode and dielectric layers, then dissolve a sacrificial layer so the stack curls into a multi-turn nano-roll; a 30x30 nm footprint could host a coil with 5-10x the area of a planar capacitor.
why: Multiplies area without HAR etch (facts 1, 4) using only nitrogen chemistry; risk is that controlled rolling below 100 nm is unproven.

title: Eliminate deposition-plus-etch: patternable metal-oxo resist becomes the capacitor dielectric
idea: Eliminate separate dielectric deposition and etch: coat a Hf- or Zr-oxo-cluster photoresist, expose it with 365-nm UV LEDs or e-beam (no excimer laser), develop it, and anneal the remaining pattern into dense HfO2/ZrO2 that stays in place as storage dielectric and node isolation, so the resist is the device.
why: Removes ~3-4 process steps per cell layer (fact 4 capital) and the neon-dependent ArF exposure; risk is the density and leakage of resist-derived oxide vs ALD.

title: Eliminate the pillar: quantum-paraelectric SrTiO3 reaches giant permittivity at 77 K
idea: Eliminate the 3D capacitor by using temperature: SrTiO3 is a quantum paraelectric whose permittivity climbs from ~300 at room temperature to thousands near 77 K, so an LN2-cooled planar SrTiO3 capacitor grown by MOCVD or hybrid MBE (no argon) stores the ~1-2 fF that 77-K retention requires on a flat ~30 nm pad. The helium ban steers us to the one cryogen that still unlocks this.
why: Removes the AR 60-75 etch entirely (facts 1, 4) on top of the cryogenic retention gain (fact 3); risks are thin-film dead layers cutting k 5-10x and k falling under DC bias.

title: Eliminate the leakage tail in place: on-die electrothermal annealing of weak cells
idea: Eliminate retention-weak tail cells without furnaces or forming-gas and argon anneals: drive a short high current through selected wordline segments so Joule heating takes the local access transistors to ~300-400 C for microseconds, annealing the interface and junction traps behind variable-retention-time and GIDL tail cells; the controller targets the cells its retention profiler flags.
why: Shrinks the <=13 fA leakage tail (fact 3) so the refresh interval can stretch 4-8x, using no process gases at all; risks are thermal disturb of neighbors and wordline electromigration.
